findings.claim: When GPT-4 generates text, it assigns probabilities to every possible next word.
findings.issue: GPT-4 is used in the present tense as the representative frontier model, but as of the publication date (2026-07-05) it is heavily superseded. OpenAI's current frontier model is GPT-5.5 (released April 23, 2026), following GPT-5, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4; even GPT-4.5 was scheduled for retirement from ChatGPT on June 27, 2026. The sentence is mechanistic (illustrating softmax probabilities) rather than an explicit 'current best model' lineup claim, so it is not blocking, but swapping GPT-4 for a current model (e.g. GPT-5.5) or framing it generically ('when a large model generates text') would avoid a dated impression on an LLM-education site.

findings.claim: As of 2026-07-05 that frontier belongs to OpenAI's GPT-5 line and Anthropic's newest Claude models.
findings.issue: Accurate and not stale, but for precision: as of the publication date (2026-07-05) the actual newest releases are OpenAI's GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna, announced June 26, 2026) and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28) plus Sonnet 5 (June 30) and the access-restricted Mythos 5 / Fable 5 (June 9-12). The article's generic phrasing ('GPT-5 line', 'newest Claude models') is correct and safe; noting only in case editors want to name current versions. Not blocking.

findings.claim: Alibaba has also moved into proprietary territory - Qwen 3.7-Max, a closed-weight, API-only flagship with a 1M-token context, was announced in May 2026.
findings.issue: Correct. Qwen3.7-Max was unveiled May 20, 2026 at the Alibaba Cloud/Apsara Summit as a closed-weight, DashScope-API-only flagship with 1M context. Verified and current. (Included only to confirm; no correction needed.)
